findings.title: Remove debug logging that dumps full ID lists at Error level
Revert cleanup ticker interval change from 10 minutes to 1 minute
Build the inline SQLite IN-list in linear time
Register DB cleanup before creating test data

response:
## 1) Severity: HIGH | Type: Performance
Title: Remove debug logging that dumps full ID lists at Error level

Affected:
- pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/xorm_store.go:534-537
- pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/xorm_store.go:554-557
- pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/xorm_store.go:576-579

Explanation:
These six log calls look like leftover debugging, and they cause real harm in production:
- **Wrong level.** Every batch logs at `Error` level, even on success. This floods error logs and can trigger error-rate alerting.
- **Huge payloads.** Each call logs the entire `ids` slice, which can hold up to `AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize` entries (the new test uses 32767). Each batch can therefore write hundreds of KB to the logs.
- **Pointless field.** The pre-delete logs include `"err", err`, which is always nil at that point because the error was already checked above.

Remove these calls, or downgrade them to `Debug` and log only counts.

Proposed fix:
~~~go
ids, err := r.fetchIDs(ctx, "annotation", cond)
if err != nil {
    return 0, err
}
return r.deleteByIDs(ctx, "annotation", ids)
~~~

## 2) Severity: MEDIUM | Type: Bug
Title: Revert cleanup ticker interval change from 10 minutes to 1 minute

Affected:
- pkg/services/cleanup/cleanup.go:77-77

Explanation:
The cleanup job interval drops from 10 minutes to 1 minute. No commit message explains this, and it looks like a leftover from local testing.

The change makes all cleanup jobs run 10x more often, not only the annotation cleanup. That includes snapshots, temp files, expired sessions and dashboard versions. The extra runs add DB load and lock contention, which works against the stated goal of avoiding MySQL deadlocks.

If a shorter interval is intended, make it configurable and justify it.

Proposed fix:
~~~go
ticker := time.NewTicker(time.Minute * 10)
~~~

## 3) Severity: MEDIUM | Type: Performance
Title: Build the inline SQLite IN-list in linear time

Affected:
- pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/xorm_store.go:609-613

Explanation:
The SQLite inline path builds the ID list with a repeated `fmt.Sprintf("%s, %d", values, v)`. Each iteration copies the whole string built so far, so the cost is O(n²).

With batch sizes in the tens of thousands, which this path exists to support, that means gigabytes of copying and heavy GC churn per batch.

Use `strings.Builder` or `strings.Join` instead.

Proposed fix:
~~~go
parts := make([]string, len(ids))
for i, v := range ids {
    parts[i] = strconv.FormatInt(v, 10)
}
sql = fmt.Sprintf(`DELETE FROM %s WHERE id IN (%s)`, table, strings.Join(parts, ","))
~~~

## 4) Severity: LOW | Type: Test
Title: Register DB cleanup before creating test data

Affected:
- pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/cleanup_test.go:116-127

Explanation:
`t.Cleanup` is registered only after `createTestAnnotations` and the count assertions have run. If any of those calls `require`/`FailNow`, the cleanup never gets registered.

All subtests share one DB, and data is inserted with fixed IDs starting at 1. Leftover rows would therefore cause duplicate-key failures and wrong counts in every later subtest, hiding the original failure.

Register the cleanup first.

Proposed fix:
~~~go
t.Run(test.name, func(t *testing.T) {
    t.Cleanup(func() { /* delete annotation + annotation_tag */ })
    createTestAnnotations(t, fakeSQL, test.createAnnotationsNum, test.createOldAnnotationsNum)
    ...
~~~
